overall_reason: A stock AI-builder SaaS skeleton (pill badge, two-tone centred hero, trust-chip row, 10 identical icon cards, 1-2-3 steps, equal tool cards, dark CTA band, link-farm footer with dead social links) with no brand, voice or proof of its own; the 'Made in Bolt' badge confirms the origin.

findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: sections run pill badge + centred hero with blue second line -> trust chips -> equal feature-card grid -> 'How it works' 1-2-3 steps -> 'Featured tools' equal 3-up cards -> dark rounded CTA band 'Ready to find your stack?' -> 4-column footer. 7 stock sections in stock order, so the read is generated despite real tool names.
findings.before: Hero / chips / 10-card grid / 3 steps / 6 cards / CTA band / footer
findings.after: Lead with the product itself: put the three-question picker in the first screen and show a real resulting stack, cutting the 'How it works' and CTA bands that only restate it.
findings.why: Specific nouns on a default skeleton still read as a default page.

findings.where: 'What are you trying to accomplish?' grid, 1440 tile 00-01
findings.evidence: Failed T-DELETION: all ten goal cards ('Study smarter', 'Start a YouTube channel', 'Build a website'...) carry the same blue concentric-target icon in a tinted tile. Removing it loses nothing; it does not even distinguish the goals.
findings.before: Identical target icon tile above every goal heading
findings.after: Drop the icon tile, or give each goal a meaningful mark (e.g. the 2-3 tool logos that goal resolves to).
findings.why: A repeated placeholder icon is the clearest sign nobody chose the decoration.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME / T-MIRROR: 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' and 'Stop browsing endless directories... AI tools that actually fits your goal, budget, and skill level' stay true for any AI-tool recommender (Futurepedia, There's An AI For That quiz). The brand is literally the category name, 'AI Stack', with a stacked-layers glyph.
findings.before: "Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack."
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: what this recommender knows or does that directories don't, e.g. who curates the 20 tools and on what test] stated in the head.
findings.why: Nothing on the first screen belongs to this business; Concept capped at 5.

findings.evidence: Twitter, GitHub and LinkedIn icon links all have href="#" (dom-1440.json).
findings.after: Link real profiles or remove the 'Connect' column: [DATA NEEDED: actual social URLs].
findings.why: Dead social links are template residue and imply a presence that does not exist.

findings.evidence: Failed T-THREE-LINE: '20+ curated tools', 'Instant results', 'Updated for 2026' with shield / bolt / trend icons are not picturable, not falsifiable and not only-this-business; they are the stock trust-chip row. The page itself later says 'A few of the 20 tools', so '20+' is also padding.
findings.before: "20+ curated tools · Instant results · Updated for 2026"
findings.after: One concrete proof line, e.g. [DATA NEEDED: who reviewed the tools and when], or remove the row.
findings.why: Generic reassurance chips are a default hero accessory.

findings.where: section heads and CTA band, 1440 tiles 01-02
findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: 'What are you trying to accomplish?', 'How it works / Three questions. One personalized stack.', 'Ready to find your stack?' would fit any quiz-funnel site; the fragment pair 'Three questions. One personalized stack.' is a stock cadence.
findings.after: Replace with a head that carries information, e.g. a sample result: 'A YouTube starter stack: [tools], [price]/mo'.
findings.why: Headings that fit any site add length without telling the reader anything.

findings.evidence: Six equal tool cards with initials avatars ('GP', 'Cl', 'Ge', 'Px', 'Cv', 'EL') in brand-ish colours instead of logos, the same yellow 'Freemium' pill on every card, and identical 'Free / ₹1,650 mo' pricing on four of six.
findings.before: Initials-in-a-square avatars and a 'Freemium' badge repeated six times
findings.after: Use the real tool marks and drop the badge where every item has it; differentiate cards by what the tool is for in this stack.
findings.why: Generated directories default to initials avatars and repeated status pills; the repetition carries no information.

strengths: The tool cards do name real products with concrete use tags and local-currency prices (₹), which is more specific than a generic feature grid.
The goal list ('Start a YouTube channel', 'Freelance', 'Grow a blog') speaks in user tasks, not features.
not_investigated: The 'Find My Stack' quiz flow and result page (only the home route was captured).
Whether prices are current: '₹1,650 mo' may be accurate conversions; not verified.
